quote: "Combine qualitative information and quantitative information to deliver some results."
title: 1. Qualitative & Quantitative Synthesis
note: Flawless C2 executive collocation. Pairing qualitative context with quantitative data is the exact vernacular boardrooms and venture capitalists listen for.

quote: "So like this, we don't need to split our resources... and that we can more focus on the sales driving factors."
title: 2. Sales-Driving Factors
note: Sharp commercial compound noun. Captures the strategic discipline of isolating core revenue levers rather than scattering operational bandwidth.

quote: "We have a lot of obstacles. But in the end, we can overcome all the obstacles and grow the business by ourselves."
title: 3. Overcoming Obstacles & Ownership
note: Natural, confident phrasing demonstrating emotional resilience and high agency — framing friction not as failure, but as a stepping stone to autonomous growth.

quote: "Asymmetrical... communication / information asymmetry between the boss and me."
title: 4. Asymmetrical Information
note: Brilliant recall and application of advanced organizational economics vocabulary. Demonstrates sophisticated conceptual thinking about management reporting bottlenecks.

quote: "What I learned is I always need to put myself in their shoes, which is seeing the situation from his angle."
title: 5. Put Myself in Their Shoes
note: Spontaneous, natural use of the British/American idiom 'put yourself in their shoes'. Shows acute upward empathy and emotional intelligence.

quote: "I give clear direction, but only the big picture and delegate all the tasks to them... I don't like to do micro-management, so I trust my subordinates."
title: 6. Autonomy & High-Trust Delegation
note: Authoritative articulation of modern executive management. Expresses trust-based autonomy and macro-level direction with clarity and poise.
